stem:
One method of producing hydrogen from natural gas is the reaction between hydrogen sulfide and methane.

$$2\text{H}_2\text{S}(\text{g}) + \text{CH}_4(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{CS}_2(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}_2(\text{g})$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write the expression for $K_{\text{p}}$ for this reaction, and state its units.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The initial partial pressures of the two gases in a mixture at $1000\text{ K}$ are recorded.

$\text{H}_2\text{S}(\text{g})$  $200\text{ atm}$  $\qquad$  $\text{CH}_4(\text{g})$  $100\text{ atm}$

The mixture is left to reach equilibrium.

It is found that the equilibrium partial pressure of $\text{CS}_2(\text{g})$ is $2\text{ atm}$ and that of the remaining $\text{CH}_4(\text{g})$ is $98\text{ atm}$.
parts.text: Calculate the equilibrium partial pressures of $\text{H}_2\text{S}(\text{g})$ and $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the value of $K_{\text{p}}$ at this temperature.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Predict the sign of $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ for this reaction. Explain your answer.

$$2\text{H}_2\text{S}(\text{g}) + \text{CH}_4(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{CS}_2(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \qquad \Delta H^{\ominus} = +241\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The free energy change, $\Delta G^{\ominus}$, for this reaction at $1000\text{ K}$ is $+51\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Calculate the value of $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ for this reaction, stating its units.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: How would the value of $\Delta G^{\ominus}$, and hence the spontaneity (feasibility) of this reaction change as the temperature increases? Explain your answer.
